task: Add `codemie analytics sync bootstrap`: a lead-side 8-step resumable Power Automate setup wizard (Teams/SharePoint link parsing, Windows time zones, flow template fill and zip package, trigger URL validation with test send, include-external/lookback choices, cross-shell install command) plus a non-interactive `--webhook` mode.

key_reasoning.reason: Several new components inside the analytics sync subsystem: bootstrap runner with deps seam, 8-step resumable wizard with saved lead state, Teams channel link parser, SharePoint folder parser, Windows time-zone list, flow-template filler, dependency-free zip writer, cross-shell install-command quoting, plus CLI registration in createSyncCommand and reuse of shared sync helpers (sendWebhook, validateInstallOptions helpers made public, buildInstallCommand, redactSecrets). Many components but one subsystem, so L rather than XL.

Closest pattern is the external collector (setup.js, links.js, zip.js, flow-template.js) plus in-repo runner/deps convention, so the port path is known. But the existing buildInstallCommand is POSIX-only quoting and does not cover the cmd/PowerShell injection surface (a trigger URL carries &, %2F, sig=); no in-repo util covers that, so the security-divergence auto-bump and sanitization floor of L apply. Also: sig validation absent in CLI, secret redaction across new outputs/state, state-file collision risk with collector's analytics-setup.json, asset shipping of JSON template has weak precedent.

Roughly 7+ new source modules (bootstrap, wizard, links, timezones, flow-template, zip, lead state) plus 5 flow-template JSON assets, and modified files: analytics/index.ts, install-command.ts, config-store.ts, possibly webhook-target.ts, package.json files and/or scripts/copy-plugins.js, docs/COMMANDS.md, docs/ANALYTICS-REPORT.md, and pinned tests (install-command.test.ts, analytics-sync-cli.test.ts). New-file count exceeds the XL band; modified count sits near L, scored XL overall.

red_flags_applied: Technical Risk bumped from M to L: closest pattern (POSIX-only buildInstallCommand) does not cover the cmd/PowerShell quoting injection surface for the webhook URL; no reusable util exists (sanitization floor of L also satisfied). Secret-redaction requirement is covered by existing redactSecrets/webhookHost, so no further security bump applied.
